receptor_A.family: Receptor tyrosine kinase (Tyr protein kinase, insulin receptor subfamily)

receptor_B.family: Type I cytokine receptor (gp130 family, IL-6 receptor subfamily)

step_1_receptor_engagement.co_expression_verdict: Both receptors pass in aged muscle. INSR is robustly expressed in old MF-I (pc=0.50, me=1.04) and MF-II (pc=0.30, me=0.62). LIFR is robustly expressed in old FB (pc=0.42, me=0.73). Co-expression in the same cell type in old is moderate (FB: INSR pc=0.22 me=0.31, LIFR pc=0.42 me=0.73), but both are clearly present in the aged muscle microenvironment. MuSC expression is detectable but low for both (pc~0.14-0.16).

linker_geometry.implications: Short flexible linker forces close proximity (~20 Å between ECD C-termini). INSR ECD=731aa, LIFR ECD=789aa — well-matched lengths. The short GS4 linker will bring the INSR kinase domain (aa 1023-1298) into close apposition with the LIFR intracellular domain (aa 859-1097) and its associated JAKs (JAK1/JAK2/TYK2). This favors transphosphorylation of LIFR tyrosines by INSR kinase and JAK-mediated phosphorylation of INSR.

pdb_evidence.INSR: 90 PDB entries available (e.g. 3BU3, 5HHW, 4IBM — insulin-bound ectodomain and kinase domain structures)
pdb_evidence.LIFR: 6 PDB entries available (e.g. 8D74, 3E0G — LIFR-IL6ST complex structures)
pdb_evidence.heterodimer_pdb: No INSR-LIFR co-structure exists (expected — they are not natural binding partners)

kinase_competence.INSR_kinase: Active tyrosine kinase domain (aa 1023-1298). Can transphosphorylate LIFR intracellular tyrosines.
kinase_competence.LIFR_kinase: No intrinsic kinase domain. Constitutively associated JAK1/JAK2/TYK2 provide kinase activity. JAKs can transphosphorylate INSR intracellular domain tyrosines.
kinase_competence.transphosphorylation_feasibility: HIGH — INSR kinase can phosphorylate LIFR pY sites (creating STAT3/SHP2 docking sites), and JAKs associated with LIFR can phosphorylate INSR tyrosines (creating IRS/SHC docking sites). This bidirectional transphosphorylation is the mechanistic basis of forced-proximity agonism.

adaptor_rationale.transphosphorylation: STAT3 is the canonical LIFR effector — recruited to LIFR pY sites (Y981, Y1001, Y1028, Y1041). Under forced proximity, INSR kinase can directly phosphorylate STAT3 docked at LIFR, enhancing STAT3 signaling beyond what natural LIFR activation achieves. SHC1 is recruited to INSR pY-NPXY motifs (pY960, pY972) and also to LIFR via JAK-mediated phosphorylation — the close proximity amplifies SHC-GRB2-SOS-RAS-MAPK. PIK3R1 (p85) is recruited via IRS1/2 to INSR and via JAKs to LIFR — proximity amplifies PI3K-AKT. PTPN11 (SHP2) is recruited to LIFR pY sites and to IRS1/2 — amplifies MAPK. JAK2 is the primary LIFR-associated kinase and can transphosphorylate INSR at tyrosines that recruit SHC1 and IRS proteins.
adaptor_rationale.cis_background: IRS1/IRS2 are INSR's canonical docking proteins — they bind INSR pY motifs directly regardless of LIFR proximity. JAK1/TYK2 are constitutively associated with LIFR's Box1/Box2 motifs — present in both natural and novokine signaling.
adaptor_rationale.excluded: PLCG1/PLCG2 (PLCγ) are not major effectors of either INSR or LIFR — no established SH2-mediated docking at either receptor's pY sites. CBL is recruited to INSR for ubiquitination/endocytosis — the forced proximity geometry with LIFR may sterically block CBL access to its INSR binding site, suppressing receptor downregulation and sustaining signaling.

step_3a_adaptor_classification.omnipath_status: OmniPath API was unavailable (HTTP 502). Analysis based on established INSR and LIFR signaling literature.
step_3a_adaptor_classification.insr_adaptors: IRS1, IRS2, SHC1, GRB2, PIK3R1, CBL, PTPN11
step_3a_adaptor_classification.lifr_adaptors: JAK1, JAK2, TYK2, STAT3, PTPN11, GRB2, SHC1

step_3c_tf_target_mapping.omnipath_status: OmniPath API was unavailable (HTTP 502). TF-target mapping based on established literature.

key_transcription_factors.STAT3: Targets: SOCS3, MYC, BCL2, CCND1, VEGFA, JUNB, FOS. Under forced-proximity INSR+LIFR, STAT3 activation is biased toward muscle-relevant targets.
key_transcription_factors.SRF: Targets: ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, TAGLN, MYOM2. SRF is activated via MAPK/ERK downstream of SHC1-GRB2-SOS-RAS. These are the muscle structural genes that appear in P2_up (young-enriched).
key_transcription_factors.ELK1: Targets: EGR1, FOS, JUN. ELK1 is a MAPK target. Under biased signaling, ELK1 activation may be attenuated relative to natural signaling, reducing IEG expression.
key_transcription_factors.FOXO1/FOXO3: Targets: ATROGIN1, MURF1 (FBXO32, TRIM63). AKT phosphorylates and inhibits FOXO. Enhanced PI3K-AKT signaling suppresses FOXO-mediated atrophy program — this is rejuvenating.
key_transcription_factors.MEF2A/MEF2C/MYOD1/MYOG: Muscle-specific TFs. MYOD1/MYOG drive myogenic differentiation. MEF2 factors co-regulate muscle structural genes with SRF.

step_3d_crispr_support.insr_screens: Present in 30+ CRISPR screens across multiple cell lines (KBM-7, HL-60, K-562, HCT116, HeLa, etc.). INSR is a fitness gene in several contexts — consistent with its role in metabolic signaling.
step_3d_crispr_support.lifr_screens: Present in 30+ CRISPR screens. LIFR is a fitness gene in several hematopoietic cell lines — consistent with its role in LIF/IL-6 family signaling.
step_3d_crispr_support.muscle_screens: No skeletal muscle-specific CRISPR screens available in ORCS database (cancer cell line focused). This is a known limitation.

gene_direction_rationale.predicted_up_rationale: All 10 predicted_up genes are present in P2_up (young-enriched) or are established SRF targets. ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN, MYL6 are directly in P2_up. TPM2 is a tropomyosin isoform co-regulated with SRF targets. NOTCH3 is an SRF target in muscle. IGFBP7 and TIMP3 are in P2_up. ZERO predicted_up genes appear in P1_up (aged-enriched) or in the IEG/aged-marker exclusion list. This matches the WIN pattern: muscle structural genes in predicted_up.
gene_direction_rationale.predicted_down_rationale: All 10 predicted_down genes are present in P1_up (aged-enriched) or are established aged IEG markers. EGR1, FOS, JUN are canonical IEGs in P1_up. OTUD1, TXNIP, IL32, MYF5, MYH9, ASB5, CSRP3 are all in P1_up. ZERO predicted_down genes appear in P2_up (young-enriched). This matches the WIN pattern: aged IEGs and stress markers in predicted_down.
gene_direction_rationale.atlas_consistency_check: predicted_up ∩ P2_up = {ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN, MYL6, IGFBP7, TIMP3} = 8/10 overlap. predicted_down ∩ P1_up = {EGR1, FOS, OTUD1, TXNIP, IL32, MYF5, MYH9, ASB5, CSRP3} = 9/10 overlap. JUN is a canonical IEG (not in the 40-gene P1_up list but established as aged marker). TPM2 and NOTCH3 are SRF targets (not in P2_up but mechanistically justified). Zero cross-contamination between predicted_up and predicted_down sets.

mechanism_narrative: INSR+LIFR forced proximity via flexible GS4 linker creates a bidirectional transphosphorylation module. INSR's tyrosine kinase (aa 1023-1298) phosphorylates LIFR's intracellular tyrosines, creating STAT3 and SHP2 docking sites — this is the primary transphosphorylation axis. Concurrently, JAK2 (constitutively associated with LIFR's Box1/Box2 motif) can transphosphorylate INSR tyrosines, amplifying SHC1 and IRS1/2 recruitment beyond what natural INSR activation achieves. The biased output enhances JAK-STAT3, MAPK/ERK (SHC1-GRB2-SOS-RAS), and PI3K-AKT (IRS1/2-PIK3R1) signaling while sterically excluding PLCγ (no SH2 docking at either receptor) and attenuating CBL-mediated downregulation. This shifts muscle cells toward a young transcriptional phenotype: SRF-driven structural genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, TAGLN — all P2_up) are upregulated, while aged IEG stress markers (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32, TXNIP — all P1_up) are suppressed.
